subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to clearer Telegram MEDIA blocked-attachment diagnostics while #47002/#47856 own configurable root expansion, or should this issue define the canonical host-local media root policy itself?
rationale: The current code enforces an intentional security boundary, while accepting more host-local paths would change the filesystem read and upload trust model rather than mechanically fixing a parser bug.

options.title: Diagnostics here, roots elsewhere
options.body: Keep this issue focused on user-visible blocked-media diagnostics and let #47002, #47856, or the approved tools.fs.roots design own persistent root expansion.

options.title: Define root policy here
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical design item for configurable Telegram MEDIA roots, including schema, docs, security tests, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Close as designed
options.body: Declare arbitrary out-of-root MEDIA paths unsupported and rely on managed roots, existing file-read policy, or explicit message send workflows.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, roots elsewhere
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on user-visible blocked-media diagnostics and let #47002, #47856, or the approved tools.fs.roots design own persistent root expansion.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice sits closest to the outbound media access and reply-media diagnostics work in recent history.
